core_obligations: Reformulate the claim (proof lines 7110-7126): fibre products exist by (item-base-change-P), and the assertion is that the image theta-bar of the given class in H^0(Y, R^{n+1}f_{tau',*}F'|_X) is zero; consider the cartesian square with its two projections.
Apply trivial base change (proof lines 7127-7133): trivial base change gives f_{tau'}^{-1}R^{n+1}f_{tau',*}(F'|_X) = R^{n+1}pr_{1,tau',*}(F'|_{X x_Y X}).

Use the equalizer hypothesis (proof lines 7134-7143): if pr_1^{-1}theta = pr_2^{-1}theta then the section f_{tau'}^{-1}theta-bar is zero, because pr_1^{-1}theta visibly maps to zero in H^0(X, R^{n+1}pr_{1,tau',*}(F'|_{X x_Y X})).

Conclude by the sheaf property (proof lines 7138-7145): by (item-restriction-A) the restriction F'|_X lies in A'_X, so by (item-A-and-P) the object G' = R^{n+1}f_{tau',*}(F'|_X) lies in A'_Y and hence satisfies the sheaf property for tau-coverings by (item-A-sheaf); since {X -> Y} is a tau-covering, the restriction G'(Y) -> G'(X) is injective, so theta-bar is zero.
proof_roadmap: Rewrite the class as a section of a higher pushforward and bring in the cartesian square.
Use trivial base change and the equalizer condition on the two pullbacks to see that the section becomes zero on the double cover.
Conclude by the sheaf property of the pushforward, which holds because the coefficients lie in the subcategory A'_Y.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a class in the equalizer of the two pullbacks on the double cover restricts to zero on a tau'-covering (statement lines 7089-7107). The proof (proof lines 7109-7145) rewrites the class as a section of a higher pushforward, applies trivial base change to the cartesian square of f, uses the equalizer hypothesis to make the pulled-back section vanish, and concludes by the sheaf property of the pushforward, which follows from the coefficient subcategory lying in A'_Y. H2: one base change computation plus one sheaf-property argument, written out.
